chunks: And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Khul'a and the Mubarayah are an irrevocable divorce, and he is a proposer from the proposers.

key_terms.الْخُلْعُ: Khul'a, compensatory divorce initiated by the wife
key_terms.خَاطِبٌ: Proposer, one who initiates the proposal of divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of Khul'a and Mubarayah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that Khul'a and Mubarayah are legally equivalent to a single, irrevocable divorce (Talaqah Bain), meaning the wife cannot remarry the same husband without an intervening marriage. This ruling classifies the husband as one of the 'proposers' (Khuttab) who initiates the separation, a nuance that distinguishes these mutual dissolutions from standard unilateral divorces in Shia jurisprudence. This classification carries significant practical implications for the waiting period (Iddah) and the conditions for remarriage.

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Khul’a and the disavowing is an irrevocable divorce, and he is a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 7. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Al -Khul‘ and al-Mubarat (denouncing) is of the kind of divorce which makes the parties become strangers to each other and he becomes one of those who may propose marriage.’”
